$comment: Single source of the installation steps: the setup wizard on the manual site (data/install.json there) and INSTALLATION.md (python tools/gen_install_guide.py).
choices: the questions asked first. Each option id can appear in a step's or block's 'when'.
when: {choice id: [option ids]}. Every listed choice must match (AND); any option in a list matches (OR). No 'when' = always.
vars: {{name}} in any text. Each var depends on one choice: 'values' per option, 'generic' when the choice is open (the Markdown guide).
steps: {id, title, nav (short title for the step list, optional), when, body: [blocks]}. Step order is the order here.

blocks (one type key each, plus an optional 'when'): p, h (sub-heading), ol / ul (list of strings), note + optional kind (info | important | coming), copy (list of {label, value}: exact strings with a copy button), table (list of [label, value]), faq (list of {q, a: [strings], when}), actions (list of {label, href, primary}).
Inline markup in any string: **bold**, `code`, [text](href), [[BUTTON]] (a hardware button), {{var}}. An href starting with # points into the manual site.
guide: the sections of the Markdown guide, one per route, each with the 'when' that picks its steps.

licensing: the release-day switch (docs/LICENSING-SETUP.md). While it is false, steps marked "licensing": true are left out of the wizard and the Markdown guide, and the manual site's header shows no Licence link.

Windows: zero install (src/_MaschineCore/zero_install.py). Live loads the script by itself on NI's own port for the controller. The customer sets nothing in Live's MIDI settings. tests/test_install_guide_zero_install.py checks the names and messages against the code.
title: Install and set up
intro: Three quick questions, then a few short steps. It takes a few minutes, and there is nothing to set up in Live.

options.label: MASCHINE MK3
options.hint: Not yet tested on a real unit

surface.generic: Maschine Mikro MK3 (MIKRO MK3) or Maschine MK3 (MK3, MASCHINE+)

ni_port.generic: Maschine Mikro MK3 (MIKRO MK3), Maschine MK3 Ctrl MIDI (MK3) or Maschine Plus Ctrl MIDI (MASCHINE+)

track_input.generic: Maschine_Mikro_MK3 Input (Maschine Mikro MK3) (MIKRO MK3) or Maschine_MK3 Input (Maschine MK3 Ctrl MIDI) (MK3)

update_copy.generic: Copy the new download's **Remote Scripts** folder into Live's User Library, as when installing.

values.win11: Drag the new download's **Remote Scripts** folder onto Live's **User Library**, as when installing.
values.win10: Drag the new download's **Remote Scripts** folder onto Live's **User Library**, as when installing.
values.macos: Copy the three folders from the new download's **Remote Scripts** folder into it, as when installing.

about.generic: On the MIKRO MK3, [[MASCHINE]] then **About** shows the new version.

scripts_path.generic: Documents\Ableton\User Library\Remote Scripts (Windows) or ~/Music/Ableton/User Library/Remote Scripts (macOS)

body.p: This version (v2) is made for **Live 12**. For **Live 11**, use **v1.6.1**: it is included in the same download, and it has its own manual.

body.note: Moving to Live 12 later? Come back here and choose Live 12: v2 is part of the same purchase.

ul: **Ableton Live 12** (12.0 or newer: Suite, Standard or Intro).
**NI's MASCHINE software**, installed (from Native Access). It installs the drivers and NI's background helper that the controller needs. You don't have to open it.
Your **{{device_name}}**, connected to the computer by USB.
The zip file from your purchase.

body.p: Nothing else. No other drivers, no extra MIDI tools, no Controller Editor templates.

body.note: Use MASCHINE+ in controller mode, connected to the computer by USB.
On Windows, the MASCHINE+ doesn't show Live's pages on its screens yet, and its pads don't play notes into Live's tracks yet. The buttons, knobs and lights work.

Support for the {{device_name}} is built from the hardware protocol and has not been tested on a real unit yet. If something doesn't behave as described, please get in touch through the [product page](https://payhip.com/b/h4tva).

steps.title: Copy the script into Live's User Library

ol: Unzip the download. It holds a folder called **Remote Scripts**.
Drag the whole **Remote Scripts** folder onto Live's **User Library** folder, below.
Windows says a folder with that name already exists: choose to merge them, and to replace the files if it asks.

body.note: No **Remote Scripts** folder in your User Library yet? The drag simply creates it. Either way, its three folders `_MaschineCore`, `Maschine_Mikro_MK3` and `Maschine_MK3` end up in **User Library\Remote Scripts**, whichever controller you have.

ol: Open the **Remote Scripts** folder inside it. It holds three folders: `_MaschineCore`, `Maschine_Mikro_MK3` and `Maschine_MK3`.
Copy **all three** into the **Remote Scripts** folder of Live's User Library, below. If that folder doesn't exist yet, create it.

body.note: Copy all three folders, whichever controller you have: `_MaschineCore` is shared. They go directly inside **Remote Scripts**, not into a sub-folder.
Moved your User Library? Live shows where it is in **Settings → Library**.

Upgrading from v1.6? v1 and v2 shouldn't run at the same time. In Live's **Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI**, set v1's control surface `Mikro_Mk3_Unofficial` to **None**. If you forget, the controller reminds you.

ol: That's it. Live finds the script by itself, and the controller's screen and pads light up.

body.p: You don't set anything in Live's MIDI settings. Live picks up the script on the controller's own NI port and remembers it.

body.note: In Live's **Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI** you can see it: the Control Surface **{{surface}}**, with Input and Output **{{ni_port}}**. Leave that row as it is.

body.p: You don't set anything in Live's MIDI settings. Live selects the control surface by itself.

body.note: If macOS asks for permission for **MaschineBridge** (Input Monitoring), allow it.

The bridge isn't notarised by Apple. A downloaded zip carries macOS's download flag (quarantine), which would block the bridge the first time. So before Live starts the bridge, the script removes that flag from the bridge's own files in `_MaschineCore/bridge`. It changes nothing else on your Mac and needs no password. Live's log notes how many files it cleared. If macOS still says it can't verify **MaschineBridge**, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

body.p: Until this computer is activated, the controller shows **Activate your key**. You do this only once per computer.

ol: Press the encoder on the controller. The activation page opens in your browser.
Enter the licence key from your purchase email, and the email you bought with. Click **Activate**.
The controller says **Activated**, and Live connects within a few seconds.

body.note: Your browser may ask whether the page may talk to apps or devices on this computer. Choose **Allow**: that lets the page reach MASCHINE for Ableton Live on this computer, and nothing else. Without it the page can't activate.

Your key is checked once with the store you bought from. The page talks only to MASCHINE for Ableton Live on this computer. If your browser can't reach it, use the page on this computer instead: **127.0.0.1:47923** (the controller shows it too).

ul: **MIKRO MK3**: for the MASCHINE MIKRO MK3.
**MK3, MASCHINE+ & MIKRO MK3**: for all three controllers.

body.p: Once activated, it works offline too. It checks itself online now and then. A computer that stays offline for 90 days is asked to go online once.
While Live is running, open the activation page, click **Connect**, then **Deactivate this computer**. That frees its place for the new computer. A key works on 3 computers.

steps.title: Live's pages on the MK3's screens

body.p: The screens show Live's pages by themselves. NI's own software draws them for the script, so there is nothing to switch or install.
On Windows, the MASCHINE+'s screens keep MASCHINE's own pages for now.

The first time Live starts with the controller, the screens switch to Live by themselves. Live's status bar says so. When Live quits, MASCHINE and Komplete Kontrol get the screens back by themselves, even after a force quit.

body.note: Is a Komplete Kontrol keyboard connected too? Then the screens stay with MASCHINE, so the keyboard keeps its own screens.

body.p: While Live starts, the controller's screen says **Waiting for Live**.
When Live is connected, the controller shows Live's screen and the pads light up. Press [[PLAY]] or hit a pad to try it.

body.note: Pads flashing in odd colours? The controller is in NI's MIDI mode: press {{midi_mode}} to leave it. You don't need MIDI mode with this script.

faq.q: The screen stays on “Waiting for Live”
a: Restart Live.
Is NI's MASCHINE software installed? It brings NI's port that Live uses for the script.
In Live's **Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI**, look for the Control Surface **{{surface}}**. Missing, or set to **None**? Choose it in an empty row, and set its Input and Output to **{{ni_port}}**.

faq.q: The screen stays on “Waiting for Live”
a: Restart Live.
If macOS asked about **MaschineBridge**, allow it (Input Monitoring, or **Open Anyway** in **System Settings → Privacy & Security**).

faq.q: Live's status bar says “no connection to the Maschine Bridge”
a: Check that the controller is connected by USB, then restart Live.
If it stays, check that the three folders are directly inside **Remote Scripts**.

faq.q: The pads play no notes, and the controller says **Tick Track**
a: Live doesn't listen to the controller's port for notes. Someone turned its **Track** switch off.
In Live's **Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI**, under **MIDI Ports**, turn **Track** on for the input **{{track_input}}**. Live's status bar names it too. Live remembers it.

faq.q: The controller says **Notes stopped** and **Restart Live**
a: The pads' notes stopped after a controller was unplugged or plugged in while Live was running.
Restart Live to bring them back.

faq.q: The controller says **Notes blocked** and **NI update?**
a: NI's software no longer passes the pads' notes to Live. This can happen after an update of NI's software.
Look for an update of this script. Until then, v1.6.1 from the same download works.

faq.q: Live's status bar says “NI's helper is off”
a: Restart the computer.
If it stays off, reinstall your NI software with Native Access.

faq.q: The controller says **Old v1.6.1 is on** and **Set it to None**
a: v1.6.1 of this script also runs in Live. Both would drive the controller.
In Live's **Settings → Link, Tempo & MIDI**, set the Control Surface **Mikro_Mk3_Unofficial** to **None**.

faq.q: Live shows the control surface twice
a: Live may have added a second row with the same control surface. Set the extra rows to **None**.

faq.q: The pads flash in odd colours
a: The controller is in NI's MIDI mode. Press {{midi_mode}} to leave it.

faq.q: I use NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) in Live, for example for the Expansions
a: Keep it in your set. While Live runs, the controller stays with Live, and the plug-in doesn't take it.
The pads still play the plug-in, like any instrument on the track. Its browser and pages work with the mouse.

faq.q: I want to play the MASCHINE Expansions without the plug-in
a: Press [[BROWSER]] and open **MASCHINE Kits**: your Expansions, then their kits. On Live 12.0 to 12.3 the kits are prepared once, in the background, the first time (**Preparing kits** with a percentage on top of the list); a kit you push before then loads by itself in a moment.

Turning onto a kit plays its preview (with preview switched on in Live's browser). Pushing the encoder loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, or a new one when an audio track is selected. The controller stays with Live.
More in [BROWSER: browse and load](#browser).
Is NI's MASCHINE software installed? It installs the drivers.
Is the controller connected by USB?
Are the three folders directly inside **Remote Scripts**?
Restart Live.

body.p: Get in touch through the [product page](https://payhip.com/b/h4tva), and attach the bridge's log file:

steps.title: You're set: how to use it

body.p: Live remembers the setup. From now on: connect the controller, start Live, play.

ul: [[PATTERN]]: your clips on the pads. Hit a pad to launch a clip.
[[PAD MODE]]: the track's Drum Rack on the pads. [[KEYBOARD]]: notes in Live's scale. [[CHORDS]]: chords in key.
Hold [[SHIFT]] for the second function printed on a button, and for the edit functions on the pads.
[[PLAY]] starts and stops Live. Hold [[NOTE REPEAT]] and a pad for note repeat.

body.note: Close the MASCHINE app while you use the controller with Live: both would try to drive it. The MASCHINE plug-in inside Live is fine.

ol: **Close Live.** The bridge closes with it.
In Live's **Remote Scripts** folder, below, delete the three folders `_MaschineCore`, `Maschine_Mikro_MK3` and `Maschine_MK3`. Delete them first: copying over them can leave old files behind.

body.note: Everything else stays: your settings and favourites and Live's control surface settings. Nothing to set up again.
